title: Authentication basics

spans.text: Authentication checks who made a request; authorization decides what that identity may access. A bearer-token API issues a short-lived token at a real login endpoint and validates it on protected routes.

`OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl="token")` tells API documentation where clients request a token and extracts bearer tokens from later requests. By itself it does not create `/token`, verify a password, or validate a JWT; the snippet below is deliberately not a complete login system.

spans.code:
oauth2_scheme = OAuth2PasswordBearer(tokenUrl="token")

@app.get("/users/me")
async def read_users_me(token: str = Depends(oauth2_scheme)):
    # Concept only: token presence does not prove identity.
    ...

spans.text: STEP 2 — WORKING PASSWORD AND JWT FLOW

Install `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `httpx`, `python-multipart`, `PyJWT`, and `pwdlib[argon2]`. Set `SECRET_KEY` to a randomly generated secret and `DEMO_PASSWORD` in the environment; never put either value in source control. Save the server code as `app.py`. Start the development server with `uvicorn app:app --reload` (`--reload` is for development only).
POST `/token` with form fields `username` and `password`; the endpoint returns a signed token that expires after 30 minutes. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to `GET /users/me`.

The example hashes the environment-provided demo password with the recommended Argon2 configuration and validates JWT signature, algorithm, and expiration. A production service must load stored password hashes from a database, use a managed secret, apply authorization checks, rate-limit login attempts, and use HTTPS.

spans.title: SECURITY
spans.text: Never store plaintext passwords or commit secrets. JWT payloads are signed, not encrypted; do not put passwords or other sensitive data in them. Rotate exposed signing keys and use HTTPS in deployed systems. The app hashes the demo password at startup; a real service stores only the resulting hash and manages accounts separately.

spans.title: TESTING
spans.text: Append the TestClient block to the same `app.py` file, set the two environment variables, and run `python app.py`. The `if __name__ == "__main__"` guard keeps those checks from running when Uvicorn imports the app.
PRACTICE: RUN THE SUCCESS AND FAILURE CASES

The following is only the additional client-test code; append it to the same file after the app code. It checks a successful login and profile request, a wrong password, a missing token, and an invalid token.

spans.code:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

    with TestClient(app) as client:
        bad_login = client.post(
            "/token",
            data={"username": DEMO_USERNAME, "password": DEMO_PASSWORD + "wrong"},
        )
        login = client.post(
            "/token",
            data={"username": DEMO_USERNAME, "password": DEMO_PASSWORD},
        )
        assert bad_login.status_code == 401
        assert login.status_code == 200

        token = login.json()["access_token"]
        profile = client.get(
            "/users/me", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}
        )
        missing_token = client.get("/users/me")
        invalid_token = client.get(
            "/users/me", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer invalid"}
        )
        assert profile.status_code == 200
        assert missing_token.status_code == 401
        assert invalid_token.status_code == 401

        print("login:", login.status_code)
        print("profile:", profile.status_code, profile.json())
        print("missing token:", missing_token.status_code)
        print("invalid token:", invalid_token.status_code)

login: 200
profile: 200 {'username': 'ada'}
missing token: 401
invalid token: 401

spans.text: Exercise: shorten the token lifetime for a local test and confirm that an expired token is rejected. Restore the 30-minute setting afterward.
